Term Availability scrape-availability.js

Queries Northeastern's official Banner SSB system (nubanner.neu.edu) to build a per-course offering history for the last 3 academic years. The output drives the "Offered In" column and the semester availability display in the app.

Script
scripts/scrape-availability.js
Output
public/northeastern/term-history.json
Rate limit
500 ms between Banner requests (override: BANNER_DELAY_MS=200)
Duration
~5–10 min depending on Banner response times

What it does

Banner SSB requires a four-step session flow to query course sections. For each term, the script must activate the term first, then fetch results in pages of 500:

sequenceDiagram participant S as Script participant B as Banner SSB S->>B: GET /classSearch/getTerms (seed session cookies) Note over S: determines which of the desired term codes Banner has available loop For each term (last 3 AYs × 4 suffixes) S->>B: POST /term/search?mode=search (activate term) S->>B: POST /classSearch/resetDataForm (clear state) loop Pages of 500 S->>B: GET /searchResults/searchResults?pageOffset=N B-->>S: {data: [{subject, courseNumber, ...}], totalCount} Note over S: collect unique courseId = subject+number end end Note over S: build term-history: only for courses in catalog

Term code format

Banner uses YYYYSS codes where YYYY is the academic year end year and SS is the semester suffix:

SuffixSemesterExample
10Fall202510 = Fall of AY 2024–25
30Spring202530 = Spring of AY 2024–25
40Summer I202540 = Summer I of AY 2024–25
60Summer II202560 = Summer II of AY 2024–25

The script queries the last 3 academic years: currentAYEnd - 3 through currentAYEnd (4 AY end years × 4 suffixes = up to 16 terms), then cross-checks against what Banner actually has available before querying.

Output format

// public/northeastern/term-history.json
{
  "CS3500": { "202510": true, "202530": false, "202540": false, "202560": false, ... },
  "CS4500": { "202510": true, "202530": true,  "202540": false, "202560": false, ... }
}

true = the course had at least one section offered that term. false = the script found no sections. Courses with no Banner history at all (catalog-only courses that have never been offered) are omitted from the file entirely.

Why courses can be missing from term-history.json

  • The course was never offered in any of the queried terms (too new, or inactive).
  • The course exists in the catalog but not in Banner SSB (e.g., placeholder or archived listing).
  • A Banner page fetch failed mid-run for that term — the script logs a warning and continues.

Usage

node scripts/scrape-availability.js            # dry run — prints summary to stdout
node scripts/scrape-availability.js --write    # writes term-history.json + change-log entry
BANNER_DELAY_MS=200 node scripts/scrape-availability.js --write  # faster (riskier)

Via the Trigger tab: ▷ Preview runs without --write and streams the summary. ⚡ Run locally runs with --write and logs a manual-trigger entry.
